Element Energy Limited (2018). Industrial Fuel Switching Market Engagement Study, final report for the Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy (BEIS), December 2018 (published 2019; with Jacobs per the 2020 CCC report citation). Cambridge: Element Energy.

Loaded: Appendix 7.2 assumption tables (TRL 2018, lifetime, fuel input per unit thermal output, reference size, marginal capex, marginal fixed opex) for 24 technologies, and the Appendix 7.3 technology data sheets (TIC capex with components, fixed and variable O&M, efficiency or COP, lifetime, TRL, maximum size, temperature limits) for 21 technologies, with the counterfactual (gas boiler, furnace, kiln, glass furnace, BF/BOF, coke plant) values printed in each sheet loaded as separate technologies. Not loaded: variable opex of the assumption table (printed rounded to 0.000/0.001 GBP/kWh; the sheets give GBP/MWh); blast furnace, BOF and sinter plant rows (no costs, placeholder 1.18 input); fuel prices, cost curves and net present costs (Figures 9-20 are charts); sensitivity table 7.4; Table 11 emissions savings. Locator: printed page numbers (PDF page = printed page + 3). Price year: the report does not state one (costs are compared in real terms discounted to 2030); 2018 used and flagged. Capex basis: sheet TIC values are installed costs; the assumption table 'marginal capex' equals the sheet TIC where both exist, except for the electric steam boiler (120 vs 200), plasma heater (262 vs 750), microwave 'H2 fired kiln' (732, equals the MAGF kiln). Capacity basis: kW of fuel input ('fired', LHV) for combustion technologies, kWe for electric units, kWth for heat pumps; kW-per-product conversions are the coordinator's. Traps: (1) fixed opex in the assumption table is about 2x the sheet O&M for electric technologies (e.g. electrode boiler 2.40 vs 1.2, plasma 2.98 vs 1.5), both loaded; (2) counterfactual rows in several sheets are shifted or mislabelled (ceramic kiln 'Fuel cost' 2.1 GJ/t brick, 'O&M' = heat duty/0.85; glass 'Efficiency 1.4 MWh/tonne' is the gas furnace SEC); (3) counterfactual BF capex is 130 GBP/t in the hydrogen reductant sheet and 387 GBP/t in the HYBRIT sheet; (4) data sheet 'range of applicability' text for the small biomass boiler repeats the large-boiler range. Year note: title page reads December 2018 and the to-get row says 2019; id element-energy_2018_001 used (printed date). The assumption table's substitution rates and maximum sizes are in _other-values. No flows or measures file.
